title: SageHaven SeqLen & Burst Readiness Assessment
next_steps: Redwood to run 1-day token/sec benchmark with SageHaven sample prompts
Send SOC2 + VPC deployment checklist and dedicated pricing options
Schedule Dedicated vs Hosted cost-run review next week
action_items: Daniel Ortiz: set up benchmark harness and request sample prompt set (due: 2027-06-03)
Amy Chen: share Dedicated pricing sheet and security pack (due: 2027-06-01)
Priya Rao / Marcus: provide seq length distribution and expected concurrency numbers (due: 2027-06-02)
summary: Initial technical discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming use-cases, token/sec burst behavior, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment suits their compliance needs. Customer wants an on-ramp pilot with a short benchmark using realistic seq lengths.
topics: p95 targets and what they mean for streaming chat
sequence length distribution and KV cache implications
deployment tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
[00:00] Amy Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Amy from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this. we've got Daniel from our SE team. can you do quick intros?
[00:10] Priya Rao: hi i'm priya, cto at sagehaven, we run several customer-facing chat assistants for claims and underwriting.
[00:16] Marcus Bell: marcus, infra lead, i look after their cloud and on-prem infra.
[00:20] Elena Soto: elena, product, i'm owning the roadmap for the conversational products.
[00:25] Daniel Ortiz: hey all, daniel ortiz, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll dig into latency and throughput.
[00:30] Amy Chen: great. quick agenda: we want to understand your p95 targets for streaming chat, the burst concurrency you expect, typical seq lengths, and any compliance constraints that push you toward private or dedicated.
[00:45] Priya Rao: yeah our big ask is p95 under 400ms for short streaming replies for auto-suggestions; for longer assistant responses we can accept up to 1.5s p95. that last part is fuzzy but the interactive paths need to feel snappy.
[01:05] Marcus Bell: to add, our peak concurrency for the chat assistant is around 220 concurrent users during business hours, but nightly batch spikes can cause token bursts for batch summarization jobs — those can hit 6k tokens/sec for a minute.
[01:25] Elena Soto: typical user utterances are short, 8-20 tokens, but system prompts plus context range sequence lengths 600-1,800 tokens depending on case. we also sometimes pin a 4k context for legal review flows.
[01:45] Daniel Ortiz: okay that's really helpful. quick clarification: when you say p95 400ms for streaming, is that end-to-end with network, or server-side generation only?
[01:55] Priya Rao: ideally end-to-end; we know network varies so we want the server-side to be sub-200ms for the short paths so total is under 400ms in our atl-east region.
[02:10] Amy Chen: makes sense. two immediate tradeoffs: hosted optimized for fast time to value but you lose some network determinism; dedicated gives you reserved capacity and more predictable p95s, private adds control for VPC/HSM but increases ops surface area.
[02:28] Marcus Bell: security is important — SOC2 is non-negotiable, we need KMS integration and audit logs. private would be ideal, but we need a realistic cost delta and runbook.
[02:38] Daniel Ortiz: understood. from a runtime perspective, for streaming short-token responses we focus on continuous batching and prefix caching to shave p95. KV cache hits reduce effective computation when users repeat context or resume threads.
[02:52] Priya Rao: do you support partial KV persistence between sessions? some of our cases reuse prior context heavily.
[02:58] Daniel Ortiz: yes, we have KV cache strategies — ephemeral and cross-request cache — but persistence across sessions depends on deployment and retention settings. that works for dedicated and private with customer-managed storage. hosted has TTL-based caching.
[03:12] Elena Soto: curious about sequence length performance. you said prefix caching helps, but we have flows that jump to 4k. what happens to p95 at those lengths?
[03:20] Daniel Ortiz: generally latency scales with seq length almost linearly for the generation step; but kernel selection and quantization impact it too. with 2k+ tokens we'll see higher tail. for p95 at 4k, unless we use model truncation or smaller context windows, we should plan higher p95. can you share the distribution?
[03:38] Marcus Bell: we'll pull distribution — most queries < 2k but 5-10% touch 3-4k.
[03:45] Amy Chen: good. for benchmarks, would you prefer us to run a hosted quick-run or spin up dedicated nodes for a like-for-like?
[03:52] Priya Rao: start hosted to validate token/sec expectations, but we want dedicated results for tail-latency and predictable p95.
[04:00] Daniel Ortiz: that's our recommendation too. hosted for fast profile; dedicated for SLA-aligned tests. we'll run a 1-day token/sec benchmark with your real prompt set — that will capture average tokens/sec, 95th percentile latency, KV cache hit assumptions, and concurrency saturation points.
[04:18] Priya Rao: perfect. what about burst handling — you mentioned autoscaling — will the autoscale respond fast enough for minute-long 6k token/sec bursts?
[04:26] Daniel Ortiz: autoscale has configured ramp and warm pools. we usually recommend a baseline reserved capacity with burst buffer that can absorb 1–2 minute surges; otherwise you need pre-warmed dedicated instances. for minute-long bursts, a warm pool or burst tokens reservation is typical.
[04:40] Marcus Bell: so we'd want dedicated with burst pool?
[04:43] Amy Chen: likely yes given your burst profile and compliance needs. dedicated gives you guaranteed capacity and faster scale characteristics, and private gives more networking control but adds ops.
[04:53] Elena Soto: cost question — any ballpark for dedicated vs hosted for our scale? rough is fine.
[04:58] Amy Chen: rough: hosted per-token plus gen costs is simplest for pilot — but for sustained concurrency and heavy bursts, dedicated with reserved GPUs can be 30–50% cheaper depending on quantization and batching. we'll run a cost model in the next step.
[05:15] Priya Rao: ok good. one more: streaming behavior — do you stream partial tokens back to client? our client shows intermediate suggestions and needs stable p95s for first byte.
[05:24] Daniel Ortiz: yes we support streaming with first-byte p95 optimizations; we can configure lower-latency paths for short responses which prioritize fast first-token emission. that sometimes increases cost per token slightly.
[05:36] Marcus Bell: about network/storage — we need VPC peering and KMS integration, and logs shipped to our SIEM. how mature are those integrations?
[05:44] Amy Chen: we've done VPC peering and customer-managed KMS with several insurers. we'll send the deployment checklist and audit log examples. private gives you full on-prem options with HSM but requires more onboarding time.
[05:58] Elena Soto: what are typical onboarding timelines?
[06:02] Amy Chen: hosted pilot can be 3–5 days; dedicated with reserved capacity 2–3 weeks; private on-prem or air-gapped usually 6–8 weeks depending on procurement and network reviews.
[06:14] Priya Rao: procurement can move fast if we have a clear SLA and security pack.
[06:19] Daniel Ortiz: for the benchmark i'll need: 1) sample prompt set, 2) seq length distribution, 3) region preference and expected concurrency, 4) whether KV persistence is needed. can you upload that to the shared drive?
[06:32] Marcus Bell: yes i'll drop that by end of week.
[06:35] Amy Chen: recap of next steps: daniel runs the benchmark (hosted then dedicated if you want), amy will send pricing and security docs, and sagehaven will provide distributions. we'll tentatively reconvene after benchmark to review findings and cost delta.
[06:50] Elena Soto: quick question — any recommended quantization or model variant for our use? we prioritise latency but not at cost of quality for underwriting cases.
[06:59] Daniel Ortiz: we can recommend 8-bit quantized variants that keep quality for most tasks; for underwriting you may prefer FP16 on dedicated GPUs for top quality with latency tuned. we'll include suggested quantization profiles in the benchmark report.
[07:14] Priya Rao: thanks, that sounds good. can you also list any gotchas for session-based KV cache and privacy?
[07:20] Daniel Ortiz: yes, we'll note data retention, encryption at rest, and options to scrub or not persist certain keys. for private you can fully control retention.
[07:30] Amy Chen: perfect. we'll follow up with an invite for the benchmark kickoff and attach the security bundle. thanks everyone.
[07:37] Priya Rao: thanks all.
[07:40] Meeting end.
